mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate below 3.0% indicates accommodative monetary policy that lowers discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days without requiring a specific trigger event.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return distribution in periods with FEDFUNDS < 3.0% shows no statistically significant positive mean (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate exceeding 4.0% signals aggressive monetary tightening that increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return distribution in periods with FEDFUNDS > 4.0% shows no statistically significant negative mean (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in housing starts (HOUST) and real personal consumption (RSAFS) above 0.5% in the past month indicates robust consumer demand, increasing corporate earnings expectations and driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both rise > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return distribution in periods where HOUST and RSAFS both rise > 0.5% in 1 month shows no statistically significant positive mean (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
